newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa produces new flag for renamed Zaire.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa produces new flag for renamed Zaire.

text.p: A South African company has begun producing a new flag for the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire, to mark the takeover of Africa's third largest country by Laurent Kabila's forces.
"We have to keep abreast of the world," Mike Clingman, managing director of the Johannesburg-based National Flag Company, told Reuters.
The first batch of 100 flags went on sale in South Africa this week, but there is no guarantee the flag will be endorsed by the new rulers.
"There's still a little bit of confusion out there in the world as to which is the correct flag," Clingman said.

The company has chosen to manufacture the flag adopted by the old Democratic Republic of Congo four years after the country gained independence from Belgium in 1960, rather than the original star-spangled emblem.

Independent Congo's first flag -- displayed by Kabila's rebels since the early stages of their guerrilla campaign -- is mainly blue and yellow with one large star in the centre and six smaller stars representing its six original provinces.
The country now has nine provinces. Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL) has not yet taken a decision to redraw boundaries.

"Mr Kabila has said he will go back to the constitution and symbols of 1964," Clingman said. "Based on that, we are assuming the flag we are making is the right one. The Zairean embassy here seems to agree because it has already bought some."

The flag being made in South Africa is a blue field bearing a yellow star in the upper left corner and a yellow-bordered red stripe running from the lower left corner to the upper right corner. It retails at 195 rand ($44).

Kabila arrived in Kinshasa on Tuesday night after his forces took the capital at the weekend, completing a stunning seven-month drive from the eastern border to topple Zaire's once all-powerful dictator, Mobutu Sese Seko.
Mobutu had renamed the country as Zaire in 1971. His flag showed an arm carrying a burning torch, in a circle surrounded by a green background.

Clingman said his company, which makes flags for numerous African countries including Namibia, Zambia and Kenya, had not yet received orders for its flag from Kinshasa but expected to make sales once Kabila announced his government.
Telephone lines at the former Zairean embassy in Pretoria went unanswered on Wednesday. The flag representing Mobutu's Zaire was removed from the embassy building earlier this week.
